title: GitHub Copilot Review 2026: Is It Still the Best AI Coding Assistant?
author: Malaclyde
description: We tested GitHub Copilot for 30 days across real projects. Here's how it compares to Cursor, Amazon Q, and other AI coding assistants — with pricing and real code examples.
content:
AI coding assistants have become essential developer tools. GitHub Copilot, launched in 2022, was the pioneer — but in 2026, it faces serious competition from Cursor, Amazon Q Developer, and Codeium. We spent 30 days stress-testing Copilot on real projects to see if it still holds the crown.

What Is GitHub Copilot?

GitHub Copilot is an AI pair programmer that integrates directly into your IDE (VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim, and more). It suggests code as you type, generates entire functions from comments, and can now hold a conversation about your codebase with Copilot Chat.

Key features in 2026:

  • Code completions: Real-time suggestions as you type in 50+ languages
  • Copilot Chat: Ask questions about your codebase, explain complex functions, refactor code
  • Pull request summaries: AI-generated PR descriptions
  • Code review: AI-powered code review suggestions
  • Terminal assistance: Explain and fix CLI errors
  • Multi-file editing: Edit across multiple files at once

Where GitHub Copilot Excels

1. Language Support

Copilot supports more languages than any competitor — 50+ including niche ones like Solidity, R, and Fortran. If you work across multiple tech stacks, Copilot is the safest choice.

2. Speed

Copilot's completions appear faster than any alternative. When you're in flow state, that 100ms difference adds up to a noticeably smoother experience.

3. GitHub Integration

Deep integration with GitHub means Copilot understands your repos, issues, pull requests, and Actions. The PR summary feature alone saves 10-15 minutes per pull request.

Where It Falls Short

1. Multi-File Context

Unlike Cursor, which understands your entire project structure, Copilot primarily looks at the current file. For complex refactoring across files, Cursor has a clear edge.

2. Price

At $10/month (Individual) or $39/user/month (Business), Copilot is in the middle of the pack. Cursor Pro is $20/month. Amazon Q offers a free tier for AWS users.

Pricing

  • Free: 2,000 completions/month, 50 chat requests/month (limited)
  • Individual: $10/month — unlimited completions, chat, PR summaries
  • Business: $39/user/month — code review, policy management, audit logs
  • Enterprise: Custom pricing — IP indemnity, SAML SSO, custom models

Verdict: Should You Use Copilot in 2026?

Use GitHub Copilot if: You work in multiple languages, want the fastest completions, and already live in the GitHub ecosystem.

Use Cursor instead if: You work on large codebases and need multi-file context awareness for complex refactoring.

Use Amazon Q if: You're heavily invested in AWS and want a free tier option.

Our recommendation: Start with Copilot Individual ($10/month). It's the most well-rounded option for most developers. If you hit context limitations, supplement with Cursor for complex refactoring sessions.
